THE TRANSCRIPTION AND THE SECTION MODEL ARE UNCHANGED: source.txt is byte-identical to 1.0.0's (sha256 5b565a958fca3e9ca5127ae9bc8439a448bfd6c0ea7a6d6cae7cc568207e7a49), base.json is CARRIED unchanged, and no find and no reading of any rule moves — not one byte of the served reading view or of /plain changes. What changes is the SCOPE RECORD of this edition's SEVEN unscoped multi-fire rules.

THE READING-VIEW-FOLD GATE (tools/fold-probe.mjs, added at 1.0.7 of the Theology of Plato) reported these seven as unscoped multi-fire rules and PINNED the count (7) as "reported, not fixed: a separate version and DOI are a separate decision". The decision has been taken, and all seven are now ADJUDICATED ON MEASUREMENT rather than by shape — every site of every one of them read off the print itself:

  r0012 "cold ness" -> "coldness"  (2 sites)  scope "all"
  r0013 "de scending" -> "descending" (2)     scope "all"
  r0014 "Capri corn" -> "Capricorn"  (2)      scope "all"
  r0015 "Phcedrus" -> "Phædrus"       (3)      scope "all"
  r0016 "Phcedo" -> "Phædo"           (2)      scope "all"
  r0017 "Timceus" -> "Timæus"         (4)      scope "all"
  r0133 "situa tion" -> "situation"  (2)      scope "all"

THE SPLIT IS 7 LICENSED "all", 0 flagged, 0 re-scoped, 0 withdrawn, and it is decided per rule on two measured tests, the same two the Theology's 117 licensed rules were decided on:

1. THE FIND FORM IS NOT A FORM THE PRINT SETS. For all seven the find occurs 0 times in the human-readable parallel of the same translation (Taylor's Select Works of Porphyry, 1823), which reads the rule's own target instead. FOUR of the seven are not OCR lookalikes at all but LOST-HYPHEN LINE JOINS: the transcription carries "cold<nl>ness", "de<nl>scend", "Capri<nl>corn" and "situa<nl>tion" with no hyphen ("cold-" 0 times, "Capri-" 0 times, "de-" 0 times, "situa-" 0 times in source.txt), so the extractor joins the lines WITH A SPACE and INVENTS a two-word form the print never sets — a form no English reading can carry. The other THREE are OCR misreads of the AE LIGATURE: the transcription has 0 ae and 0 oe anywhere, while the print sets them.

2. THE PRINT ITSELF SETS THE RULE'S OWN READING AT EVERY SITE, read BLIND off the page images with the two readers this library measured as non-echoing (google/gemini-2.5-flash and anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 on 10.0.0.1:8322), each asked only to transcribe the page, the expected form NEVER named. The print's own ligature is visible on those leaves in words no rule touches ("nautae", "praesidebant", "Proserpinae", "Philologiae", "amphorae"), so the transcription's zero-ae measurement is a property of the transcription, not of the print.

NOT ONE BYTE OF THE SERVED TEXT CHANGES. That is the finding, and it is the point: the gate's pin existed because these seven multiplicities were UNLICENSED, not because they were wrong. Every rule still fires, with the same stored `fires`, and 1.0.0 is untouched and keeps its own DOI.

A FINDING FOR ANOTHER UNIT, REPORTED AND NOT FIXED HERE: this edition's page model is OFF BY ONE. derivs.json gives printed page = leaf - 6 (n14 = 8, n49 = 43), while the leaves' own running heads give page = leaf - 5 on every one of the seventeen leaves read here (n13 8, n21 16, n22 17, n32 27, n33 28, n34 29, n35 30, n39 34, n41 36, n48 43, n50 45, n53 48, n54 49, n55 50, n56 51, n57 52, n59 54, n62 57), and the leaf that actually carries a site is derivs_leaf - 1. Every leaf placed in this unit was placed by matching the site's line to the edition's own running heads, never by derivs.json. Reported, not fixed: the page model is a separate state and is not in this unit's scope.
